subject.title: tools.exec.approvalRunningNoticeMs is documented but rejected by the 2026.3.24 config schema

question: Should maintainers replace the conflicting non-editable fork repair with a narrow same-repo schema fix, ask the fork author to rebase, or keep waiting?
rationale: The bug is clear, but an open fork PR still claims the exact fix and is currently conflicting and not maintainer-editable, so automation should not silently race that candidate.

options.title: Replace With Narrow Same-Repo Repair
options.body: Open or adopt a focused target-repo fix for the schema/test change and then close the stale fork candidate as superseded.

options.title: Ask Fork Author To Rebase
options.body: Keep this issue waiting on the external fork PR, requiring the contributor to resolve conflicts and provide proof before it can land.

options.title: Keep Waiting
options.body: Leave the issue and fork PR open without a new repair, preserving the current user-facing docs/schema mismatch.

recommendation.title: Replace With Narrow Same-Repo Repair
recommendation.body: Open or adopt a focused target-repo fix for the schema/test change and then close the stale fork candidate as superseded.

likelyOwner.reason: The relevant exec config history and schema refactor history point to this area, and the decision is about target-repo repair ownership rather than the original reporter.
